title: Jerry Jones reveals when he thinks NFL expands to 18-game season, but process to get there is complicated - CBS Sports
description: Jones sees the NFL 'maybe' expanding to an 18-game regular season sooner than one might think
body:
Jones sees the NFL 'maybe' expanding to an 18-game regular season sooner than one might think
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The National Football League regular season could be expanding once again.From 1978 to 2020, the NFL played a 16-game regular season, but that changed in 2021 as the league expanded to a 17-game regular season. However, Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones, one of the league's most influential voices, feels an expansion to an 18th regular-season game is just around the corner. "I don't think we're far away from it," Jones said Friday, via 105.3 The Fan in Dallas. "What is far away? Next month? No. Next year? Next year, maybe. Next year, maybe. That has to be negotiated with the players, but it's in everybody's best interest."Why would a greater physical toll in the regular season benefit the league's players playing one of the most violent sports? Jones claims the compromise would be to trim the NFL preseason once again. Teams typically play three exhibition games as a warm-up and to evaluate the back-end depth on their respective rosters. Two teams end up playing four preseason games if they participate in the "Hall of Fame Game" centered around the Pro Football Hall of Fame enshrinements in August.Jones feels simply erasing more preseason games and having the early regular season games, which already have a preseason feeling to them, is in everyone's best interest, players included. The NFL would certainly be in a position to ask for more money on its next media rights deals with its broadcast partners in that scenario. The league signed its current 11-year, $110 billion media rights deal with CBS, FOX, NBC, ESPN/ABC and Amazon Prime Video   in 2023. 
"You would cut back on the preseason games," Jones said. "You would have teams develop more in the first few games as the type of thing you're trying to get done in the preseason, but it's in everybody's interest. It certainly is in the player's best interest, in my mind, for sure. Having said that, I would anticipate that coming."Negotiating hurdles stand in way of any changeThe league's current CBA with the players' union is locked in through the 2030 season, so any tweaks to the regular season would necessitate additional negotiation between the league and the union. Commissioner Roger Goodell didn't see an 18-game regular season on the horizon like Jones does now when he addressed the topic at Super Bowl LX in February. "We have not had any formal discussions about it and frankly very little of any informal conversations," Goodell told reporters back in February. "It is not a given that we will do that. It's not something we assume will happen. It's something we want to talk about with the union leadership."  
One league source voiced concern to CBS Sports about increased injuries in an 18-game regular season in April. That is believed to be the biggest holdup to adding an additional regular-season game. "The bigger concern is now we're going to add another game, even if you multiply everything out with sensible assumptions, there are going to be more injuries," a league source told CBS Sports in April. "And it won't just be hamstrings. There are going to be season-enders and next-season-enders in Week 18 and 19. That's the biggest sticking point on the field."  One player, who requested anonymity, also told CBS Sports in April that some of the NFL's top stars could sit out games at the end of an extended 18-game season to charge up for the playoffs or to reduce the risk of injury. 
"The NFL's issue will be more related to getting top players to play in games beyond playoff contention, which I believe get exacerbated the more regular season games they play," the player told CBS Sports in April. "Top players will check themselves out more because games that don't matter late in the season will happen more often."While Jones has been able to bring many major changes to his Cowboys and the league at large over the years, an expansion to an 18-game regular season may be a little more complicated than he thinks.

schema.headline: Jerry Jones reveals when he thinks NFL expands to 18-game season, but process to get there is complicated - CBS Sports

title: Kentucky hits last second three to avoid historic upset vs. Northern Arizona - CBS Sports
description: Kentucky needed a last-second 3-pointer to escape what would’ve been a historic loss at
body:
Kentucky needed a last-second 3-pointer to escape what would’ve been a historic loss at home
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:32 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Jordan Prather | Imagn Images
            
            

    
        Kentucky escaped a near-historic upset loss on Friday against Northern Arizona when guard Alex Wilkins knocked down a 3-pointer to give his team a 78-77 win at home. The Wildcats trailed by four points in the final minute. After NAU missed the front-end of a one-and-one, Wilkins delivered a go-ahead shot to avoid what would've been one of the most stunning losses in Kentucky basketball history. 
Kentucky led by as many as 13 in the first half before Northern Arizona mounted a comeback to take a lead in the final minutes. For the third time in three games, Mark Pope's team struggled. Kentucky were on the ropes against James Madison last week at home before pulling away late. Earlier in the week, Kentucky suffered an embarrassing loss at the Champions Classic where Pope's squad was completely outclassed by the Jayhawks. Even though Kentucky beat NAU — a team that has been at the bottom of KenPom's rankings the last few seasons — it won't ease the pressure on Pope in what is a make-or-break season for his alma mater.
Kentucky entered the 2026-27 season with one of the highest-priced rosters in the sport. Naturally, the expectations were high for the No. 24-ranked Wildcats after adding multiple transfers — including Iowa State sharpshooter Milan Momcilovic — who was the best 3-point shooter in the sport last season. After having one of the highest-priced rosters last season with a price tag reportedly over $20 million, that group underachieved and lost to Iowa State in the second round of the NCAA Tournament. From the moment last season started to the final game, Kentucky had several lowlights, including a 17-point loss to Michigan State, a 35-point loss to Gonzaga and a 25-point defeat against Vanderbilt during SEC play.
Even though Kentucky improved to 3-1 with the win over Northern Arizona on Friday night, it won't cool down the hot seat and the pressure facing Pope this season. Kentucky is expected to drop out of the next AP poll rankings after losing to Kansas. With games coming up against Indiana, Virginia and Louisville during the next month, playing as Kentucky did against NAU will result in a different result in the win-loss column.

title: Dejounte Murray landing spots: Three possible destinations after Pelicans guard requests trade - CBS Sports
description: Murray, an All-Star in 2022, has had a rough tenure in New Orleans and wants out
body:
Murray, an All-Star in 2022, has had a rough tenure in New Orleans and wants out
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:33 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        We have our first trade request of the 2026-27 NBA season. If you had Dejounte Murray on your bingo card, congratulations. The 2022 All-Star landed with the New Orleans Pelicans before the 2024-25 season, but his tenure there has been a mess and he requested a trade on Friday. He played 31 games in his first season, shooting worse than he ever had before tearing his Achilles. He returned late last season and played well, but the beginning of this season has been a mess.Murray has remained in the starting lineup for the Pelicans, but New Orleans is 1-8 in the games he's played. They've lost his minutes by over 14 points per 100 possessions, he's shot poorly from basically everywhere on the floor, and he hasn't been a consistently impactful defender since he played for the San Antonio Spurs. 
Meanwhile, Murray has made his displeasure public on several occasions.In 2025, he criticized the organization on The Pivot Podcast. "I'm not getting what I need in the organization," he said. "It's hard for me to get my training time. It's hard for me to get lifts. It's hard for me to get my own court time. So, you can only imagine where my mental was at."In a since-deleted tweet replying to clips posted by Pro Pels Talk, Murray said that fans have "no f--- ing clue what we are dealing with."Murray himself retweeted Shams Charania's tweet about his trade request, which would seemingly open him up to a fine for publicly requesting a trade.At this stage, Murray's trade value is likely minimal. If a deal comes, it will likely involve a similarly bloated, multi-year contract attached to a player that a team is eager to move. Essentially, we're looking for "problem for problem" type of trades. Three destinations make some degree of immediate sense.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Phoenix SunsThe Suns are the first team to register known interest, according to Chris Haynes. Earlier this season, Haynes reported that the team's lack of a point guard had created frustration in the locker room. Phoenix started the season 1-5, but has since won four of its last five to somewhat right the ship.
Still, the Jalen Green experience has been a borderline disaster for Phoenix. The Suns have a staggering -15.7 net rating when Green plays and a +10.2 net rating when he sits. The former No. 2 overall pick was one of the primary pieces returned in the Kevin Durant trade, but his shooting has fallen off a cliff. He provides none of the playmaking that Devin Booker needs in a backcourt mate (which is part of why the Suns have fared so much better with Collin Gillespie on the floor in his place), and his defense is mostly nonexistent.Both Murray and Green have player options for next season, with Green set to make $36 million and $30 million owed to Murray. The notoriously stingy Pelicans might insist on some form of compensation for taking on that extra money, but the premise here would essentially be the "problem for problem" structure we suggested above. With Murray gone, Jeremiah Fears could be the unquestioned starting point guard for the Pelicans. Green would either come off the bench or slot next to him at shooting guard, while Murray would be closer to the point guard archetype that Booker prefers. It's by no means a perfect fit. Murray's weakness as a 3-point shooter would be problematic as the Suns have lost quite a bit of shooting since last season, and the Pelicans frankly have too many talented, shoot-first players as is. But it's at least an attempt at addressing real issues for both sides. The rebuilding Pelicans might at least like to take a look at a supremely gifted athlete, while the Suns would hope to get the point guard they feel they've lacked.

                            
    
                                                
                    
    Miami HeatAndrew Wiggins has really struggled to fit into the new, Giannis Antetokounmpo-centric version of the Heat. The former No. 1 overall pick is averaging less than nine points per game on some of the worst shooting numbers of his career. His usually steady defense has slipped a fair bit on a unit that has been enormously disappointing as a whole, and, offensively, Miami's lack of a genuine shot-creating guard has proven problematic early in the season. The Heat need a more reliable shot-generator than Murray, but after spending most of their assets on Antetokounmpo, their options are somewhat limited. This sort of swap would essentially be a bet that going from one of the NBA's worst organizations to one of its best could rejuvenate a former All-Star. Fitting a point guard that shoots poorly from deep on a Giannis team would be pretty problematic, but Miami would presumably stagger the two of them to limit their minutes together.Such a swap would appeal to New Orleans for a few reasons. The first is contractual. Wiggins signed an unusual contract last offseason. He had a player option for the 2026-27 season, but rather than decline it and sign an entirely new deal, he picked it up and added a cheap two-year extension on the back end. He is making over $30 million this season but will dip to $16.3 million next season. That makes him an ideal trade target for a team that wants to save money. He can match salary with Murray in a trade now, but cost far less next year.
And then of course, there's the chance that Wiggins bounces back on a team that plays a bit more traditionally than Antetokounmpo-led teams can. Pelicans wings Trey Murphy III and Herbert Jones have been rumor mill fixtures for years, and with Saddiq Bey in place and a potentially rejuvenated Wiggins incoming, New Orleans would potentially feel a bit more comfortable cashing one of those other forwards out for draft picks since they'd have replacements in the building.
                            
    
                                                
                    
    Charlotte HornetsMurray is emphatically not the sort of player that the Hornets tend to target, especially at point guard. Charlotte wants to bomb 3-pointers. That is not now, nor has it ever been Murray's game. When Charlotte traded LaMelo Ball, it expected to be able to sustain a somewhat respectable offense with Coby White in his place and Kon Knueppel ascending. Well, Ball is starring in Minnesota and White and Knueppel have barely played.The Hornets knew they were taking a step back this season with the Ball trade. They probably didn't expect the NBA's worst offensive rating, highest turnover rate and lowest true shooting percentage. Bringing in Murray could at least provide them with a stabilizing force at point guard, someone who could raise the floor enough to properly evaluate everyone else on the team moving forward.
The Hornets have a $40.8 million trade exception generated from moving Ball and almost $30 million in room below the tax line. They could nearly absorb Murray outright without sending out another contract, and they've shown a willingness to take on salary in exchange for draft capital. That would be the idea here. The Hornets are not taking on Murray's player option for next season lightly. The Pelicans would have to make it worth their while with some form of first-round draft compensation. The Pelicans are probably hesitant to do so after all of the criticism they (justifiably) received for the Derik Queen trade, but Charlotte is probably the only team that can offer real financial relief for Murray at this point. If that's a priority, there might be a conversation here. If the Pelicans expect the Hornets to treat Murray as a real asset, the Hornets almost certainly pass.

title: James Madison vs. UConn live stream, where to watch online, CBS Sports Network channel finder, odds - CBS Sports
description: CBS Sports Network is home to six games in Week 11, beginning on Tuesday night
body:
CBS Sports Network is home to six games in Week 11, beginning on Tuesday night
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:58 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The stretch run of the college football season has arrived as teams jockey for position within conferences and try to get bowl-eligible in Week 11. CBS Sports Network will again have six games on the Week 11 slate, beginning with some weeknight MACtion. First up was Western Michigan at Akron on Tuesday night, where the Broncos rolled to a 42-14 win. Then on Wednesday, UMass was shut out by Toledo, 24-0, as the Rockets improved to 5-1 in the MAC.Saturday's action kicks off with James Madison traveling to UConn at 12 p.m. for an intriguing matchup, as the Dukes try to close the season strong after seeing playoff dreams vanish with a pair of recent losses. Then at 3:30 p.m., Middle Tennessee will travel to Liberty to try and knock off the Flames, who remain undefeated in Conference USA play so far in 2026. The evening slate begins in Colorado Springs (7 p.m.), where Air Force brings the Commander-In-Chief's trophy home after beating Army and has to refocus as strong favorites against San Jose State. The nightcap takes us to Pullman (10:30 p.m.) where Washington State hosts Colorado State in a battle of teams at the bottom of the Pac-12. 
CBS Sports Network will carry all six games, with full viewing info, betting lines and key storylines to follow as Week 11 unfolds.All times Eastern | Odds via SportsLine consensus   James Madison at UConnDate: Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time: 12 p.m.Location: Pratt & Whitney Stadium at Rentschler Field -- East Hartford, ConnecticutTV: CBS Sports Network [Channel finder] Live stream: CBSSports.com | Mobile: CBS Sports AppSpread: James Madison -4After back-to-back losses derailed the Dukes' dreams of back-to-back playoff appearances, James Madison got back to winning ways by demolishing Southern Miss on the road last week. Now they'll travel up to Connecticut to face a Huskies team still trying to claw their way to bowl eligibility after getting thumped by UNC last Saturday. The 8-2 Dukes are short road favorites over the 4-5 Huskies, with the latter running out of time to get to six wins on the season. 
Middle Tennessee at LibertyDate: Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time: 3:30 p.m.Location: Williams Stadium -- Lynchburg, VirginiaTV: CBS Sports Network [Channel finder] Live stream: CBSSports.com | Mobile: CBS Sports AppSpread: Liberty -20.5The Flames got off to a slow start last week but eventually pulled away for a comfortable win in Las Cruces, remaining undefeated in Conference USA this season. Now they return home to face a Middle Tennessee squad that's fresh off a shootout win over Western Kentucky and is now one win away from bowl eligibility for the first time since 2022. Getting that this week will be a tall order for Derek Mason's Blue Raiders as they're three-touchdown underdogs on the road, but if they did pull a shocking upset, it'd be the biggest win of his tenure in Murfreesboro. San Jose State at Air ForceDate: Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time: 7 p.m.Location: Falcon Stadium -- Colorado Springs, ColoradoTV: CBS Sports Network [Channel finder] Live stream: CBSSports.com | Mobile: CBS Sports AppSpread: Air Force -11.5
The Falcons improved to 7-2 on the season and collected the Commander-In-Chief's trophy last week in a thrilling victory at Army. Securing the CIC makes this a successful year for Tim Calhoun's bunch, but they still have business to attend to in the Mountain West. The Falcons need help, but at 3-2 in conference play, they aren't out of the championship game picture just yet. First up, they will need to refocus after beating Army and take care of a Spartans team that's 3-3 in Mountain West play following last week's win over Northern Illinois. The Spartans gave New Mexico all they could handle two weeks ago, and if Air Force is still basking in the glow of beating Army, they could get tripped up. Colorado State at Washington StateDate: Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time: 10:30 p.m.Location: Gesa Field at Martin Stadium -- Pullman, WashingtonTV: CBS Sports Network [Channel finder] Live stream: CBSSports.com | Mobile: CBS Sports AppSpread: Washington State -9.5It's a battle of the two teams at the bottom of the Pac-12 standings in this week's nightcap, but that doesn't mean this won't be exciting. Washington State, winless in Pac-12 play so far, is more than a touchdown favorite against a Rams team that is the worst defense in college football. Colorado State allows 44.8 points per game, which is the most by more than six full points in the country. Washington State's offense is the 130th-ranked scoring offense in the nation at 19.0 points per game, but even this Cougars offense should find space to run against the Rams in what figures to be another track meet involving Colorado State.

title: FAA flight stoppage affecting Week 11 travel plans for several college football teams - CBS Sports
description: On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stoppage for all departing flights due to "ext
body:
On Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a nationwide ground stoppage for all departing flights due to "extraordinary circumstances and reasons for safety." That announcement came as numerous college football programs were preparing to leave for road games across the country.After a lengthy halt to all air travel, the FAA lifted the ground stop on Friday night, but programs still have work to do in order to finalize their travel plans. In his press conference, Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy recommended that schools reach out to the FAA about their travel arrangements."I would encourage those football teams to reach out to the FAA to schedule their flight times and make sure they have games going off tomorrow," Duffy said.As of Friday night, there were quite a few teams that haven't taken off, and they are still working on alternative travel plans. That raises another set of questions, including timing and player safety. What if these teams can't get the proper rest after spending most of Friday night on a bus, and will games have to be pushed back due to late arrivals?
Another wrinkle in all this is that on-air talent and behind-the-scenes staff for broadcasts will be affected by the groundstop. That will be something else to monitor as the chaos unfolds.As teams and conferences sort out the next steps, here is the latest on how notable Week 11 matchups have been affected by the FAA's groundstop.SECIn addition to sorting out which teams will be able to arrive on time for kickoff, the SEC is still assessing if any officiating crews for Saturday's games have been affected by the groundstop, sources tell CBS Sports.
The conference issued a statement on the FAA's ground stoppage on Friday night, saying it's still evaluating the situation with all member institutions.
Auburn at Mississippi StateKickoff: Moved to 4:15 p.m. from original kickoff time of 12 p.m. ETAuburn wasn't able to get off the ground before the FAA issued the stoppage, but the Tigers will take a bus to Starkville, sources told CBS Sports. Late Friday, the SEC announced the kickoff time would be adjusted from 12 p.m. to 4:15 p.m. "due to travel issues related to Friday's FAA ground stoppage."  No. 3 Alabama at VanderbiltScheduled kickoff: 12:45 p.m. ETThe Crimson Tide already made plans to bus to Nashville and were unaffected by the stoppage, sources tell CBS Sports.
No. 8 Tennessee at Texas A&MScheduled kickoff: 3 p.m. ETSources tell CBS Sports that Tennessee will fly to its game against Texas A&M on Friday night now that the FAA has lifted its ground stoppage.No. 22 Missouri at No. 1 GeorgiaScheduled kickoff: 3:30 p.m. ETThe Tigers have arrived in Athens for their showdown against the top-ranked Bulldogs, sources tell CBS Sports.No. 19 Ole Miss at OklahomaScheduled kickoff: 4:15 p.m. ETOle Miss hadn't arrived at the airport prior to the ground stoppage and after the order was lifted, determined the Rebels would not fly to Oklahoma on Friday night. 
"We are continuing to work through our options and coordinate with the appropriate groups regarding both travel and the game," an Ole Miss spokesperson told CBS Sports.Florida at No. 11 KentuckyScheduled kickoff: 6:15 p.m. ETFlorida arrived in Lexington before the stoppage was put into place. The Gators and Wildcats are still set to square off on Saturday evening.No. 6 Texas at No. 21 LSUScheduled kickoff: 7:30 p.m. ETTexas had not departed and was sitting on the tarmac when the ground stoppage was announced, sources tell CBS Sports. The Longhorns returned to the team facility after the order was issued and went through its usual Friday hotel routine -- meetings and dinner. The Longhorns were finally headed to the airport Friday night and planned to fly to Baton Rouge. 
No. 17 South Carolina at ArkansasScheduled kickoff: 7:45 p.m. ETThe Gamecocks landed in Arkansas prior to the stoppage, sources tell CBS Sports. South Carolina is set to put its four-game winning streak on the line against the Razorbacks. Additionally, the officiating crew will be set for kickoff.Big TenSources tell CBS Sports that Washington, Minnesota and Purdue are the only Big Ten teams impacted by the stoppage. Additionally, all officials will be available for their game assignments.Northwestern at No. 20 Ohio StateScheduled kickoff: 12 p.m. ETNorthwestern has landed in Columbus, per The Athletic. The Wildcats are scheduled for a noon kickoff against the Buckeyes.
Nebraska at RutgersScheduled kickoff: 12:30 p.m. ETThe Huskers took off before the flight stoppage and have landed in Newark, New Jersey, sources tell CBS Sports.No. 18 USC at No. 9 IndianaScheduled kickoff: 3:30 p.m. ETAt roughly 2:30 p.m. ET on Friday, USC posted photos of players boarding the team plane with the caption, "in route." The Trojans took off prior to the ground stoppage.Michigan at No. 16 OregonScheduled kickoff: 3:30 p.m. ETSources tell CBS Sports that Michigan traveled to Eugene on Thursday. That decision paid dividends for the Wolverines as they were able to avoid Friday's chaos.
Washington at Michigan StateScheduled kickoff: 4:15 p.m. ETSources tell CBS Sports that Washington was grounded in Seattle. The Huskies are staring down a long trip to East Lansing with few good alternatives on Friday evening.Minnesota at Penn StateScheduled kickoff: 7 p.m. ETMinnesota was grounded prior to taking off for its game against Penn State. The Golden Gophers are expected to fly to Penn State on Saturday, a source tells CBS Sports.  Purdue at No. 15 IowaScheduled kickoff: 7:30 p.m. ETThe Boilermakers did not take off before the stoppage, but they will take a bus to Iowa City, sources tell CBS Sports.
ACCSources tell CBS Sports that all ACC schools are at the sites for their respective games. The conference is assessing its officiating situation, but the league believes it's in a good place there as well.No. 13 Wake Forest at SMUScheduled kickoff: 12 p.m. ETSources tell CBS Sports that Wake Forest has landed in Dallas for its early kickoff on Saturday. The Demon Deacons have not been affected by the ground stoppage.Cal at VirginiaScheduled kickoff: 3:30 p.m. ETThe Golden Bears have arrived in Charlottesville, sources tell CBS Sports, which is good because that would have been a long drive from Berkeley.
Boston College at Notre DameScheduled kickoff: 3:30 p.m. ETAccording to the team's social media accounts, Boston College boarded the team plane and took off prior to the ground stoppage.Stanford at Virginia TechScheduled kickoff: 7:30 p.m. ETSimilarly, the Cardinal would have had quite the trek from Palo Alto. Fortunately, Stanford made it to Blacksburg before the stoppage was implemented, sources tell CBS Sports.Big 12The Big 12 released a statement on Friday night, and the conference is evaluating all its options, including possible changes to the Week 11 schedule."Due to the national FAA ground stop impacting team travel, the Big 12 Conference is evaluating potential changes to Saturday's football schedule," the league said in a statement. "The Conference will continue to monitor the travel disruptions alongside its member institutions and provide updates for Saturday's games."Cincinnati at Iowa StateScheduled kickoff: 12 p.m. ETThe Bearcats have landed in Des Moines as they get set to play the Cyclones in the early window on Saturday, sources tell CBS Sports.Kansas State at TCUScheduled kickoff: 2 p.m. ETThe Wildcats were stuck on the tarmac at the time of the stoppage, sources tell CBS Sports. If Kansas State were to take a bus, it's just over a seven-hour drive from Manhattan to Fort Worth. The Horned Frogs have announced that they are in discussions with Kansas State about the kickoff time.Arizona State at UCFKickoff: Moved to 5:30 p.m. ET from original kickoff time of 3:30 p.m. ETArizona State faces one of the longest treks of the weekend -- more than 2,000 miles from Tempe to Orlando. Sources tell CBS Sports the Sun Devils are preparing to fly out on Saturday morning ahead of their mid-afternoon kickoff against the Knights.Baylor at BYUScheduled kickoff: 3:30 p.m. ETBaylor is grounded in Waco, and it will try to fly out on Saturday morning, per ESPN. That creates a small window to arrive in time for the game against BYU in Provo.No. 2 Utah at No. 23 ArizonaScheduled kickoff: 7:30 p.m. ETSources tell CBS Sports that the Utes will not fly out from Salt Lake City on Friday night. They will return home and try to fly out on Saturday morning. The Big 12 is expected to push back the kickoff time due to the Utes' travel issues, a source told CBS Sports.  No. 12 Texas Tech at No. 25 Oklahoma StateScheduled kickoff: 9:30 p.m. ETThe Red Raiders have landed in Stillwater, sources tell CBS Sports. The major Big 12 clash between Texas Tech and Oklahoma State is still on as scheduled.Notable group of six gamesJames Madison at UConnScheduled kickoff: 12 p.m. ETJames Madison made it to UConn prior to the stoppage. The Dukes are still slated to take on the Huskies at noon on CBS Sports Network.Tulane at RiceScheduled kickoff: Moved to 4:30 p.m. ET from original kickoff time of 2 p.m. ETSources tell CBS Sports that Tulane did not take off prior to the stoppage, but is expected to bus to Houston for its game vs. the Owls.FAU at TulsaScheduled kickoff: 3:30 p.m. ETThe Owls have been grounded in Florida as they hope to reach Tulsa for their matchup against the Golden Hurricane, sources tell CBS Sports.Oregon State at No. 24 Boise StateScheduled kickoff: 6 p.m. ETSources tell CBS Sports that Oregon State has not left for its game against Boise State. That game has major College Football Playoff implications for the Broncos, so this will be one to monitor closely.UNLV at New MexicoScheduled kickoff: 7:30 p.m. ETUNLV returned to the airport after the stoppage was lifted, as it prepared to fly Friday to New Mexico, a source told CBS Sports. The Rebels are slated to take on the Lobos in a game with major College Football Playoff implications.Utah State at SDSUScheduled kickoff: 9:30 p.m. ETThe Aggies are still in Logan as they evaluate their options ahead of a game against SDSU, sources tell CBS Sports. Utah State has some time with a Pac-12 After Dark kickoff time.NDSU at HawaiiScheduled kickoff: 11 p.m. ETGiven that flying is really the only way for NDSU to reach Hawaii, it's a good thing the Bison arrived at 5 a.m. on Friday, sources tell CBS Sports.

title: Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray requests trade after social media rants - CBS Sports
description: 'You have no f---ing clue what we dealing with,' Murray posted this week after a blowout loss
body:
'You have no f---ing clue what we dealing with,' Murray posted this week after a blowout loss
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:36 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        New Orleans Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray wants to be traded. A day after defending himself on social media in a now-deleted post that criticized his play during a 145-111 loss to the Brooklyn Nets earlier this week, the former All-Star and his representatives requested a trade from the franchise, the team announced Friday. One team that has "registered interest" in adding Murray is the Phoenix Suns, per Chris Haynes. "Today, Dejounte Murray's representatives informed us of his request to be traded," the team said. "We will evaluate potential trade opportunities that are in the best interest of our organization."ProPelsTalk, a Pelicans podcast, posted clips on social media highlighting purported mistakes Murray made during his team's fourth consecutive loss, to which Murray responded that fans have "no f--- ing clue what we are dealing with.""Ohhhhh let's talk about it," Murray posted in a now-deleted tweet. "When you run post plays, are they suppose to catch on the block or the 3pt line? Let's hear it Mr social media coach, Gm and President? You have no f---ing clue what we dealing with. Maybe you should ask the whole team individually how they feel on a serious note and then pull rethink alot of shit."Murray finished with five points, four assists, and two rebounds in 28 minutes during the loss. This season, Murray is averaging 13.4 points, the lowest since his third season in the league with the San Antonio Spurs. On the same day Murray tweeted and then deleted that tweet, he also responded to another tweet, noting that the Pelicans are 1-8 with Murray and 3-0 without him.
"From what's going on INSIDE, this sounds like someone hit you to say this!!" Murray wrote in a now-deleted tweet. "THE 'SABOTAGE' IS REAL!!"Murray appeared in just 14 games during the 2025-26 season after recovering from a torn Achilles that sidelined him for more than a year. The Athletic's Sam Amick reported on Thursday that he expects the Pelicans to have "very legitimate conversations" about Murray being moved."Dejounte (Murray), I would fully expect to have very legitimate conversations about him being on the move," Amick said. I thought that would be the case closer to the deadline. The mood certainly is the type of thing that could accelerate it."
Murray, 30, is in the final guaranteed season of his current contract. He has a player option for $30.7 million for the 2027-28 season.

schema.headline: Pelicans guard Dejounte Murray requests trade after social media rants - CBS Sports

title: Blue Jays' Anthony Santander issues statement after sharing anti-Muslim videos: 'This content caused hurt' - CBS Sports
description: Santander said he 'should have been more thoughtful' about what he shares on social media
body:
Santander said he 'should have been more thoughtful' about what he shares on social media
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:01 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander has issued a statement regarding his recent anti-Muslim social media posts that he has since deleted. Santander's statement, which he posted to Instagram and follows a public condemnation of the posts by Blue Jays general manager Ross Atkins, reads as follows: "After taking time to reflect on my recent social media posts and speaking with people I trust and respect, I recognize that I should have been more thoughtful about what I shared on my platform."I realize that this content caused hurt and I sincerely apologize. I should have been more thoughtful about what I shared, recognizing the responsibility that comes with having a public voice."As a man of faith, it is my belief that every person deserves to be treated with dignity and respect, regardless of their religion, background, or beliefs. After hearing feedback from those I hurt, I realize that the content I shared fell short of my own convictions."I would like to affirm my respect for the Muslim community and for the dignity and freedom of people of every faith and background."From this experience, I have learned to ensure that none of my communications promote hate or give the impression that I support hatred, discrimination, or violence against anyone."The club had earlier released a statement on the incident that read: "Baseball is for everyone, and the Blue Jays have created an inclusive experience where all fans feel welcome at our ballpark. Individual comments do not represent our organization's values and beliefs."Santander, a Venezuela native, shared social media videos following the recent U.S. midterm elections, including one in which a Christian pastor said, "There is no such thing as kind Muslims." Another suggested that Sharia law would be imposed in the U.S. following the election of Abdul El-Sayed to the Senate representing the state of Michigan. Atkins told reporters Tuesday that Santander's behavior "did not align" with organizational values and there were no words "to express my level of disappointment.""I talked to Anthony about his lack of awareness, realizing that he has a very large microphone, what that meant," Atkins said. "We're working exceptionally hard internally to ensure, and we have been, that it's a safe environment, that baseball is for everyone. It's very important to us. It's a part of our organizational values and his behavior did not align with that."  
Santander, 32, joined the Blue Jays prior to the 2025 season on a five-year, $92.5 million free-agent contract. He struggled badly across 54 games in 2025 and missed the entire 2026 season with injury.

The Crimson Tide travel to Nashville to take on Vanderbilt where they will reportedly start backup quarterback Austin Mack in place of Keelon Russell, who is dealing with an ankle injury, per ESPN. Russell was listed as probable on Alabama's official injury report this week after suffering an ankle injury in the Tide's win at LSU last week, but Alabama will reportedly look to get him another week to heal up as they take on one of the SEC's worst teams in Vanderbilt. Mack, Alabama's junior backup, has only thrown four passes this season -- completing three for 23 yards -- but did appear in some spot duty a year ago, throwing for 228 yards and two touchdowns during the 2025 season. Mack was under consideration for the starting job this spring, but DeBoer ultimately rolled with his talented sophomore in Russell, which has proven to be a wise decision. 
Alabama's offense has been dynamic this season with Russell under center, as his abilities not only as a passer but as an elusive scrambler have made the Tide incredibly hard for defenses to corral. With Mack, the Tide figure to be less dynamic but will have a quarterback with plenty of familiarity with the offense being in his third season in Tuscaloosa. The Tide have been 15.5-point favorites for most of the week, but the report of Russell sitting and Mack starting saw the line move a point in Vanderbilt's direction to 14.5 -- but still shows plenty of confidence in Alabama to handle the Commodores on the road. 
If Alabama is able to get a win over Vanderbilt as the odds would suggest, they will face Chattanooga at home next week in another game they could rest Russell if they wanted to ensure his ankle had extra time to heal. The Iron Bowl closes out the season for the Tide and then they will hope to shift their attention to the final SEC Championship Game and the College Football Plaoyff with Russell at full strength.

title: Trinity Rodman leads surging Spirit against breakout Royals in NWSL semifinal - CBS Sports
description: With the championship match set for D.C., Trinity Rodman and company can secure a home final if they can halt an
body:
With the championship match set for D.C., Trinity Rodman and company can secure a home final if they can halt an underdog Utah squad riding high after stunning San Diego
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:56 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NWSL playoffs roll on with the semifinal round, and fans will be treated to a glimpse of the future site of the 2026 NWSL Championship. Audi Field in Washington, D.C., has a way of making regular-season games feel even bigger, and on Saturday it hosts another penultimate chapter ahead of the final.This will be the third home semifinal at Audi Field in as many years, and the third-place Washington Spirit will host the eighth-place Utah Royals (on CBS, noon ET), with a chance to play at home in the NWSL Championship on Nov. 21. A neutral site is chosen for the NWSL Championship annually, and this year's Audi Field announcement was made back in June, setting in motion endless possibilities for the Washington Spirit to have an all-home playoff run.But they're going up against the breakout team of the year in the Utah Royals, a team that finished in 12th place last season, with only six wins. Now they've spent the 2026 regular season creating new club history and are coming off a huge quarterfinal upset over the second-place San Diego Wave.Here's everything to know about the big game:Playoffs run through Washington SpiritThe Spirit's long season had highs, some lows and plenty of plateaus. While the Spirit at one point looked like prime contenders for the NWSL Shield, they let it slip away to eventual winners Gotham FC with two games remaining in the season.
But the NWSL playoffs are a different beast. A three-game gauntlet to claim the big prize, where the only real thing that matters is the best form over a short span of matches. There's no better time to make a statement than the quarterfinal round, and both the Spirit and Utah delivered.The Spirit's 4-1 demolition of the Portland Thorns was a showcase of their skill, but also of how the group is fueled and functions at home. Trinity Rodman scored twice and added an assist, as Portland were outclassed on the pitch between their giveaways and the Spirit's breakaway chances."They're steaming now. They're going now, which is obviously what you want. A team that starts really high performing in the playoffs," Utah head coach Jimmy Coenraets said about the Spirit.
"I think the biggest difference is that you go to Rowdy Audi, which I think, looking at the Portland [quarterfinal], within two minutes it scored two goals based on just the whole crowd getting behind them. So I think it's being smart about momentum, it's being smart about timing and stuff. Maybe sometimes killing the game slightly more, and then just being smart about a few things."Rodman is the headliner of the Spirit's roster. She finished the regular season with a career-best 12 goals and eight assists, was named an NWSL MVP finalist this year and has carried that form into the postseason. A massive bright spot for the Spirit is also the overall player depth.Despite player movement and injuries, the group seems to be hitting its stride in the playoffs, especially with newcomers Melissa Bethi and Clara Lavunga, who joined midseason. Both players scored in the quarterfinal and could prove to be the difference-makers for the Spirit after three consecutive semifinal appearances. Alongside other players who are now staples of the club -- defender Tara Rudd and midfielder Andi Sullivan, the longtime team captain -- the group is not trying to get ahead of itself with the possibility of playing a championship at home. First, the Spirit have to tackle the semifinal.
"I can't even go there in my mind. Like, you know, everyone's talking about the final being here, but again, we have a semifinal, so you can't get to there yet. But obviously, we want to be there, so that's definitely motivation to get the job done," Sullivan said on "Attacking Third." 
"The rotations of players coming in and out, and whether that's due to injuries or new signings or whatever it may be, and I just think that's a testament to, like, the locker room and the closeness we have in the locker room ... and I think that's what we're really like leaning on into this playoff push."Utah Royals' successful turnaroundClubs hoping to change their fortunes will look to Utah as a blueprint. After a 6-13-7 record and 12th-place season last year, and 11th place in 2024, the group is now navigating its first-ever playoff appearance.
Head coach Jimmy Coenraets, who was recently nominated for NWSL coach of the year, had been the interim coach before taking over the team permanently in October 2024. Mina Tanaka's more elevated play, along with the return of veterans like Cloe Lacasse and Paige Monaghan, helped turn the page for Utah in 2026. Signing Miyabi Moriya and Kiana Palacios and trading for Narumi Miura were also key offseason moves.While the group spent the second half of the season winning one week and losing the next, the playoffs offered a reset. With locker-room belief and a "why not us?" attitude as the eighth-seeded playoff team, Utah delivered the biggest upset of the postseason with a cagey 1-0 win against the second-place San Diego Wave. It was Palacios who provided the game-winning goal, after receiving the setup from Lacasse. 
Goalkeeper Mandy McGlynn is also on fire for the Royals. She racked up crucial saves throughout the quarterfinal and is rallying the team into D.C. She has previous experience winning the 2023 NWSL Championship with the former eighth-place Gotham FC side. Coenraets believes her experience and the team's camaraderie on the road will be huge in Saturday's mental test.
"I think that's how you create your own momentum. So when you're going against, I don't know how many it will be, 20,000, 22,000 [at Audi], you have to ... like it's impossible to cancel the noise, but you just got to create your own noise. You've got to make sure that players feel the energy from the sideline, from players and staff. I think that's the biggest message, because again, it will be loud, and I have to say I was impressed last week listening to [how] loud they were. But again, like you have an opportunity to create your own momentum, and I think that's what we want to do tomorrow," he said.What's nextThe Washington Spirit will host the Utah Royals at Audi Field in Washington, D.C., on Saturday. The winner of Saturday's semifinal will face the winner of Sunday's semifinal between Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current. The final two teams will face off in the NWSL Championship on Nov. 21 on CBS.

schema.headline: Trinity Rodman leads surging Spirit against breakout Royals in NWSL semifinal - CBS Sports

title: Eagles release wide receiver Hollywood Brown upon his request, according to report - CBS Sports
description: Brown wasn't used much in the Eagles offense this year
body:
Brown wasn't used much in the Eagles offense this year
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:19 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Philadelphia Eagles are reportedly releasing wide receiver Hollywood Brown at his request, according to a report from ESPN's Tim McManus. The team and Brown agreed to terms on a non-injury settlement that offers financial relief to the Eagles, the report states.Brown has not been utilized much on Philly's offense. Playing in just four games with one start, Brown saw just eight targets for five receptions -- all first downs -- for 63 yards and no touchdowns. He also had two additional rushing attempts for 12 yards.The Eagles offense has had its fair share of struggles across the board, and injuries have been a major storyline for the team. They are set to get wide receivers DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks back soon after being sidelined with injuries, so the need for Brown has diminished even further.The wide receiver room also includes Makai Lemon, who has led the team the last three weeks in receiving yards and leads the team in total receiving yards (312), and Darius Cooper.
Brown was initially brought to Philadelphia to help relieve pressure on the pass game after A.J. Brown was traded to the New England Patriots during the offseason. The 8-year veteran signed a one-year, $5 million deal with Philadelphia, his fifth team since entering the league in 2019. The move clearly didn't work the way either side wanted, and despite injuries, the Eagles offense didn't ever feel a need to lean on Brown.Back in October, the 29-year-old discussed not being on the field as much as he expected. "I wouldn't have handled it well as a younger guy," Brown said during the late-October media availability. "... It's God's plan, and the more I got comfortable with that, I can't be mad about a situation because maybe that's not what God called for. ... Of course, you want to be somewhere where you play, but at the end of the day, it's not my plan."
In his career with the Eagles, Kansas City Chiefs, Arizona Cardinals, and Baltimore Ravens, he has played in 94 games, with 73 starts, and has 376 receptions for 4,385 yards and 33 touchdowns. Last season, he had 49 receptions for 587 yards and five touchdowns in 16 games for the Chiefs.

title: Vikings officially announce Kirk Cousins will start vs. Packers following trade deadline - CBS Sports
description: Minnesota traded for their old friend on Tuesday at the NFL trade deadline, and he will start for the Vikings rig
body:
Minnesota traded for their old friend on Tuesday at the NFL trade deadline, and he will start for the Vikings right away on Sunday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:48 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            2 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The Minnesota Vikings (6-2) aren't providing their old friend Kirk Cousins any ramp up before throwing him back in the fire. After trading for the 38-year-old quarterback at the NFL trade deadline on Tuesday in a deal with the Las Vegas Raiders, Cousins will start against the Green Bay Packers (6-3) on Sunday at Lambeau Field.That means he will join Cam Newton with the Carolina Panthers and Boomer Esiason with the Cincinnati Bengals as the only quarterbacks since 1950 to start for a team in a second stint after they previously won 50-plus games with said team in their first tour of duty. 
"Cannot give him enough credit for coming in here, how he's gone about the week, both him and the coaching staff getting him ready to go, using all the time we possibly can," O'Connell said during Friday's media availability. "It's been really impressive what he's been able to do and just the command and just getting right back in the huddle with a lot of guys he's played with, but certainly some guys he hasn't. It's been something that everybody's been very, very impressed by."Minnesota is desperate for the jolt the four-time Pro Bowl quarterback can provide for their sagging offense. Cousins has 22 total touchdowns in 2026, and the Vikings have scored just 11 offensive touchdowns, tied for the fewest in the NFL with the 0-8 Los Angeles Chargers. His 20 passing touchdowns rank as the second-most in the league this season, just three behind Joe Burrow's league-leading 23 and one ahead of Jordan Love's 19. 
This news certainly makes four-time Pro Bowl wide receiver Justin Jefferson's Friday a happy one. Jefferson won NFL Offensive Player of the Year honors in 2022, his last season with a fully healthy Cousins, after leading the league in targets (184), catches (128), receiving yards (1,809), and receiving first downs (83).  The 98.9 passing yards per game that Cousins averages to Jefferson is the most by a quarterback-receiver duo in NFL history (min. 50 games together).    Coach Kevin O'Connell also hopes Cousins' presence can halt the quarterback carousel Minnesota has gone through since Cousins tore his Achilles in his last Vikings start at Lambeau Field against the Packers in Week 8 of the 2023 season. They have made an NFL-high 17 starting quarterback changes since then. 
Should the Vikings hang on and make the playoffs in the 2026 season, Cousins could become the first quarterback in NFL history to start a playoff game in the same season he started a game for multiple teams.

schema.headline: Vikings officially announce Kirk Cousins will start vs. Packers following trade deadline - CBS Sports

title: Usman Nurmagomedov, five others sentenced to six months in Abu Dhabi prison for attack on Merab Dvalishvili - CBS Sports
description: Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili were also fined for the violent altercation
body:
Nurmagomedov and Dvalishvili were also fined for the violent altercation
        
        
                                                                                                            
                                                    By
                                                
                                                            CBS Sports Staff
                                                    
                    
                                    
        
    Nov 13, 2026
                            
                    at
    3:49 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            1 min read
            
        
    
            
    
            
        
                
                
                
            
        
            
                    
                Getty Images
            
            

    
        Usman Nurmagomedov is facing six months in prison following the Wednesday incident in Abu Dhabi. Nurmagomedov, along with five others involved, will also have to pay a roughly $82,000 fine and be ordered to deportation following their prison terms for their part in the altercation that left Merab Dvalishvili battered and bloodied, according to a statement from the Abu Dhabi judicial department.Nurmagomedov and his associates approached Dvalishvili and his friend at the fighter hotel in Abu Dhabi ahead of Real American Freestyle wrestling event. Video appeared to show Nurmagomedov slap Dvalishvili before the brawl ensued.
All parties involved were immediately detained by authorities. RAF CEO and co-founder Chad Bronstein announced shortly after sentencing that Dvalishvili and his friend, Saba Lazishvili, had been released from police custody. Dvalishvili released a brief statement on social media on Friday to address the matter."Just want to let everyone know I have been released and I am good, healthy and ready to go. I want to thank everyone in Abu Dhabi for your help in resolving this matter," Dvalishvili wrote. "I love visiting Abu Dhabi and am happy to be welcomed. I do hope that they release everyone -- I would not press charges. I want peace and the best for all. Thanks everyone for your love and support."
Nurmagomedov is currently a free agent who was recently signed to the Professional Fighters League and, before that, Bellator. He has been seen at recent UFC events, supporting his brother, Umar Nurmagomedov, and teammate, Islam Makhachev.

title: UFC 334: An inside look at Josh Hokit's meteoric rise to title challenger - CBS Sports
description: NEW YORK -- Depending upon the time of day or the number of people present when a microphone is placed in front of unbeaten Josh Hokit,
body:
NEW YORK -- Depending upon the time of day or the number of people present when a microphone is placed in front of unbeaten Josh Hokit, you can expect to hear from one of two sides of the rising heavyweight's contrasting personalities.There's Josh, the former Division I All-American wrestler from the blue-collar farmland of California's San Joaquin Valley, who walked on in two sports at Fresno State University and went on to sign with two different NFL teams before transitioning to MMA. Josh is a quiet and calculated competitor of the highest degree who is never lacking for confidence.And then there's "The Incredible Hok." That guy is an obnoxious handful to most and a growing folk hero to an increasingly vocal minority that can't help but pull up a chair and enjoy Hokit's character-driven journey to command our attention at any cost, regardless of the consequences. This crass version of Hokit has boldly navigated the toxic reality of elite MMA, where those who can disrupt the loudest and keep winning can cut the line in pursuit of the sport's greatest riches. Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 334 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!
Hokit (10-0) has gone from making his UFC debut last November as a little-known trash talker to headlining Madison Square Garden on Saturday against Ciryl Gane (14-2, 1 NC) at UFC 334. And whether his formula for fast-tracking ends with him becoming the heavyweight champion of the world or not, the last 12 months of Hokit's meteoric rise have been staggering to watch. On Thursday, Hokit turned 29, and he has only been a pro fighter for just over three years. In January, he fought at UFC 324 on the opening bout of the early prelims and just 10 months later -- after co-authoring the craziest fight of 2026 in an April win over Curtis Blaydes and knocking out UFC's all-time KO artist Derrick Lewis at the White House in June -- he's on the verge of legitimate breakout stardom.
This is the type of heater not seen in the UFC since Brock Lesnar won the heavyweight title in 2008 just 287 days after his debut or when Alex Pereira transitioned from kickboxing star to UFC middleweight champion in just 371 days (which, coincidentally, would be the exact amount of time between Hokit's first walk to the Octagon and Saturday's card should he capture the sport's most prestigious title).
"It's no surprise to me," Hokit told CBS Sports on Tuesday. "I keep saying this, but it takes 10 years to make an overnight sensation. So, I have been putting in the work and have been waiting for my opportunity. Every opportunity that the UFC has given me, I have made the most of it, and so now I'm being rewarded for that. We are rewarded by our courage in this life and not our intelligence. And people get that twisted. People will try to have a certain approach, but you need to go for it; you need to put it all on the line. You need to be all or nothing and that's what I'm going for."
        
            
                Ciryl Gane brushes off dirty fighter label, but others are convinced: 'All of these things are illegal'
                
                    Brian Campbell                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Not all of Hokit's comedic material lands, and much of it overshadows his true ability and the purity of his story of overachievement. But whether you respect Josh the person or loathe the cringier side of "The Incredible Hok" as a character, both have relied upon an insane work ethic and a fierce competitive spirit to get Hokit to where he is today.Hokit has accepted opportunities against more proven names on short notice and consistently rolled the dice, believing that his fearlessness and aggression could overcome his lack of experience. 
So far, Hokit's bet on himself has paid off, as he has openly benefited from being an undersized heavyweight who relies on his athleticism and quick hands to surprise and overwhelm his much larger opponents. But that doesn't mean he believes what he's doing is a template that can be easily replicated. 
"If you don't have wrestling, then I wouldn't advise it for a small heavyweight," Hokit said. "At least I have the wrestling in the back pocket, and I think wrestling is the great equalizer. So, I could always fall back on that and make the heavyweights tired. But at the end of the day, it's all about tactics and it's all about strategy. If size always played a factor in the fight, then the elephant would be the king of the jungle."Hokit's unexpected rise has been aided by the constant chaos surrounding the UFC's heavyweight division, which dates back to Francis Ngannou vacating the title in 2023 to leave the promotion as a free agent. Jon Jones returned from a 3-year layoff to win the title but sat out for more than a year due to injury and ended up retiring again in order to avoid fighting then-interim titleholder Tom Aspinall. 
Things only got crazier from there, as accidental eye pokes from Gane in their title bout last year led to Aspinall undergoing multiple surgeries before being forced to vacate the belt two months ago, during a stretch that Hokit calls "unlucky" for the division. Hokit, who is entering his fifth UFC fight in just a 12-month span, believes it's his willingness to be a "rare" active heavyweight that makes him the perfect candidate to save the division. Hokit, who began his shtick of WWE-inspired theatrics during his post-fight interviews on the regional MMA scene, initially turned just about everyone off. He made multiple tasteless jokes about seemingly unrelated celebrities, including crude remarks about former first lady Michelle Obama that drew public chastising from UFC CEO and president Dana White, and even simulated vomiting on himself while weighing in before the Lewis fight in June. 
"I kind of just put my material out there and then it's like, it is what it is," Hokit said. "Whether you like it or not, at least it's something for you to judge because I think that's real important for me. I don't want you to see my name or watch me fight, and then you don't know how you feel about me. I'm just giving everybody a lot to react to. Whether you like it or not, it is what it is."
One month earlier, during a UFC Freedom 250 press conference in Newark, New Jersey, Hokit was ejected by security after his vulgar comments about Ilia Topuria's ex-wife and Alex Pereira's mother nearly sparked fisticuffs with both fighters. Hokit's act may appear foolish and irrational on the surface, thanks to his blatant disregard for shame, but it's all part of his clever strategy to upset the entire sport in pursuit of clout, and it's hard to argue it isn't working. He even wrote the verses for his new diss track titled "MSG Freestyle," which launched complete with a music video, and took shots at the entire division."I'm here to piss people off, No. 1. And I think I'm the shit, No. 2," Hokit said. "So, that's the beauty of this sport, at the end of the day. I'm talking smack, but at least you can do something about it. You could sign the contract and fight me. Shit, if they want to fight me outside, it is what it is. I'm down for all of it. But I think we live in a day and age where people aren't like that anymore. Usually, they will have the opportunity to fight me in the cage in front of the world. We can make some money off of it."
Slowly but surely, however, the court of public opinion within MMA is starting to come around on Hokit, in ways that can be gauged not just by the social media metrics proving that the antihero side of his polarizing personality is rapidly becoming appealing to fans, but also by how many current and former UFC fighters are now openly praising him. From Daniel Cormier, Chael Sonnen and Robert Whittaker to Sean O'Malley, Jorge Masvidal and Dustin Poirier, all of them seem to have endured the same trajectory as many fans. They initially loathed Hokit before eventually coming around to realizing the method to his madness and realizing just how much excitement he brings to the division and the sport. 
"It's a crazy trajectory [Hokit] has been on," Poirier, the retired UFC star and current Paramount+ analyst, told CBS Sports on Monday. "He's walking the walk and talking the talk. When you do that, you become a superstar in this sport. I've said it over and over again. We have seen Paddy [Pimblett], we have seen Chael, we have seen Conor [McGregor]. When you do that, you become a superstar. You just have to keep winning."
Even Gane, who has found himself as the punchline of multiple Hokit zingers entering Saturday, didn't hesitate to share the respect he has for him. "As a man, [I respect him] because I know he likes to pretend that he's dark [but] this is a role, I'm pretty sure," Gane told CBS Sports on Tuesday. "And [I respect him] as a fighter; also, he did very well, 10-0, against good fighters. But he has less experience. This reminds me of when I started, a little bit. You have less experience and maybe you are less technical on the wrestling or the striking game, but you manage very well and you win the fight at the end. So, that means he has a good fight IQ." Hokit doesn't see himself as a hero or a villain when it comes to the multiple personas he has crafted. Love him or hate him, as long as you feel something, he has done his job. 
"I'm whatever the UFC needs. Whatever I am, the UFC needs it," Hokit said. "I just look at it as entertainment."One year ago, almost no one in MMA was talking about Josh Hokit. But on Saturday, in the same building that has been a cathedral of combat sports where former heavyweight champions like Muhammad Ali, Joe Frazier, Evander Holyfield, Lennox Lewis, Andy Ruiz Jr. and Jon Jones have enjoyed some of the biggest moments of their careers, "The Incredible Hok" has the same opportunity to forever link his name with history. "When you got the game upside down, full nelsoned and face on pavement, this is where I belong at the end of the day," Hokit said. "You named all those legends, and I see myself as a living legend already. My third fight in the UFC was a Hall of Fame fight, a legendary fight. So, I believe I've earned this. I've earned a chance to compete here, and I want my name to be with them."

schema.headline: UFC 334: An inside look at Josh Hokit's meteoric rise to title challenger - CBS Sports

The promotion's landmark UFC 205 event saw Conor McGregor become the first simultaneous two-division champion. Since then, The World's Most Famous Arena has hosted defining moments like Georges St-Pierre's triumphant return and Jorge Masvidal's BMF coronation.The annual New York City event is a cornerstone of the promotion. This year is no different. Josh Hokit could go from UFC debutant to heavyweight champion in 12 months by dethroning Ciryl Gane in the main event. Sign up for Paramount+ and watch UFC 334 for no additional fee -- every UFC numbered event and UFC Fight Night is included with your subscription! Plans start as low as $8.99/month or $89.99/year!Saturday's co-main event is worthy of the iconic New York City venue. Kayla Harrison is one of the most decorated women in combat sports, having won two Olympic gold medals in judo, a UFC title, and two PFL tournaments. Amanda Nunes is unequivocally the best women's MMA athlete of all time. Her resume includes wins over former UFC champions Ronda Rousey, Valentina Shevchenko (twice), Cris Cyborg, Holly Holm, Germaine de Randamie (twice) and Miesha Tate. Many factors are at play, including Harrison's first fight after career-threatening neck surgery and Nunes' return from a three-year retirement.
But Saturday night is about a lot more than just the pair of title fights atop the marquee.
        
            
                UFC 334 fight card -- Ciryl Gane vs. Josh Hokit: Five biggest storylines to follow in New York

Ahead of Saturday's loaded card, take a look at three undercard fights you can't miss.Stephen Thompson vs. Charles Radtke"Wonderboy" is heading for greener pastures. Two-time UFC title challenger Thompson fights for the final time this weekend. It's a fitting farewell for the 43-year-old, who returns to the same venue where he nearly dethroned welterweight champion Tyron Woodley a decade ago. Their memorable UFC 205 scrap earned Fight of the Night honors and might have been the evening's biggest story had McGregor not closed out the historic triple-header by becoming the UFC's first champ-champ.
Thompson remained a factor at 170 pounds for years after his two title fights with Woodley, but three straight losses signaled that his time was running out. UFC matchmakers have given him a reasonable opportunity to leave on a high note. Charles Radtke is solid competition with a 5-2 UFC record, losing only to ranked welterweights Carlos Prates and Mike Malott. Can Thompson find that "Wonderboy" magic one last time, or will he share the cruel fate that many beloved fighters do in the twilight of their careers?
Caio Borralho vs. Yousri BelgarouiBorralho is taking a considerable risk. The UFC's No. 6-ranked middleweight is coming off a victory over Reinier de Ridder, his eighth win in nine Octagon appearances. Borralho should be climbing towards a title shot, but he's agreed to defend his place among the division's elite against an unranked opponent. And not just any unranked opponent.
Belgaroui is cut from the same cloth as former UFC champions Alex Pereira and Israel Adesanya. The Dutch striker fought both men twice in kickboxing before transitioning to MMA. He now trains alongside Pereira under Glover Teixeira's tutelage. Belgaroui is a perfect 3-0 in the UFC, with all three victories coming by knockout. He's following a familiar blueprint, and Madison Square Garden is the perfect place for it. Pereira made his UFC debut at the Garden in 2021 before returning the following year to win the middleweight title. Now it's Belgaroui's turn to make a statement in NYC. But Borralho is a considerable obstacle. The Fighting Nerds' cerebral leader has the tools and experience to expose gaps in Belgaroui's developing MMA game. It's a difficult assignment for both men, albeit for very different reasons.Bilal Hasan vs. Luis GuruleHasan might be the best talent to emerge from this year's crop of "Dana White's Contender Series" graduates. "The IndoNinja" punched his ticket to the UFC with a 45-second knockout, then returned just two weeks later to score another KO in his promotional debut. Saturday marks his third fight in three months under the UFC umbrella. The young flyweight has finished nearly everyone he's faced, and should be due for another one.
Hasan hovers around a staggering -1000 favorite against Gurule, who has struggled to a 1-4 UFC record. Some might question why such an apparent mismatch belongs on a Madison Square Garden main card, but there are things to like about it. Talent development hasn't historically been the UFC's strong suit. The promotion touts competitive matchmaking, but that philosophy sometimes comes at the expense of rushing prodigies into fights they're not ready for. Hasan has the makings of a future champion, and there's no reason to hurry him towards the division's elite. Let him build his experience, collect highlights and develop into the fighter he has the potential to be. Saturday is the next step in his story.

Can Missouri slow down a red-hot Georgia team looking to protect its No. 1 CFP ranking?

        If No. 22 Missouri is going to keep its College Football Playoff hopes alive, it needs a win over No. 1 Georgia on Saturday. That's a big ask considering the lopsided history between the two programs.The Tigers had an opportunity to get a resume-building win at home against Texas last weekend, but they let a second-half lead slip away in a 34-20 loss. Now Missouri has to pick itself up and prepare for a trip to Athens. Expect the Tigers to lean on their passing game against Georgia, although star receiver Cayden Lee suffered an injury late against Texas. Quarterback Austin Simmons and wideout Donovan Olugbode can do some damage through the air.On the Georgia side of things, Kirby Smart doesn't need to change much. The Bulldogs have stomped their first two opponents out of the open date -- Florida and Ole Miss -- and are playing their best football of the season. Gunner Stockton was efficient in the passing game against the Rebels, and the run game rumbled for nearly 300 yards. The defense has forced six turnovers in the last two games, and that unit just made Trinidad Chambliss look like a bottom-tier SEC quarterback.Here's everything you need to know about this ranked showdown in Sanford Stadium.
Georgia vs. Missouri: Need to know  Mizzou looking for first win over No. 1: The Tigers have never beaten the No. 1 team in the country. Their 18-game losing streak to top-ranked opponents is the longest without a win in AP poll history. The only programs with streaks in the same zip code are Ole Miss and Pitt (15). There's no better time to change that than the present, I suppose. If Missouri can spring the upset, it would serve as a historic moment for the program and a major boost to its playoff hopes.Georgia winning with offense and defense: The Georgia defense gets a lot of credit, and rightfully so. That unit is perennially among the best in the country thanks to Kirby Smart, but the offensive output shouldn't be overlooked this year either. The Bulldogs are averaging 41.1 points per game, which ranks sixth nationally and is 0.2 points shy of the team's best mark, set in 2014. Even with questions about its passing game, Georgia is hanging enormous numbers on the scoreboard.One-sided series: It's tough to own an all-time series more than Georgia has owned this one. The Bulldogs are 12-1 against Missouri, with the only loss coming in 2013. The last two meetings -- in 2022 and 2023 -- were much closer than other recent matchups. Perhaps that means Missouri is closing the gap, but it's also hard to overlook the run from 2017-21 when the Bulldogs won five games with an average margin of victory of 27.6 points. Nobody likes to see Georgia on the other sideline, but especially not the Tigers.
Where to watch Georgia vs. Missouri live  Date: Saturday, Nov. 14 | Time: 3:30 p.m. ET  Location: Sanford Stadium -- Athens, Georgia  TV: ABC | Live stream: Fubo (try free)  Georgia vs. Missouri prediction, picks  Missouri is capable of making things interesting if Georgia lets its foot off the gas pedal after a big win over Ole Miss. The Bulldogs have already made that mistake once against Auburn. Will Kirby Smart let them make another one in this spot? I find that hard to believe. The flagship university of the Show-Me State is going to have to show me that it can beat the Bulldogs before I feel comfortable betting on them. Georgia rolls for the third consecutive week. Pick: Georgia -15.5
